    Plot phylogeny with predicted and known hosts

    plot_phylo_hosts.Rd

    This function takes a phylogenetic tree (`phylo`) and a data frame containing information on predicted and known hosts for each tip, and produces a circular (or rectangular) tree with: - Predicted hosts highlighted with bold italic labels and custom colour. - Known hosts marked with a tip point and custom colour.

    plot_phylo_hosts(
  phylo,
  pred_hosts,
  label,
  layout = "circular",
  tiplab_offset = 5,
  tiplab_size = 1.7,
  tippoint_shape = 18,
  tippoint_size = 2,
  pred_color = "darkgoldenrod3",
  nonpred_color = "gray50",
  known_color = "#cf3530",
  show_legend = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    phylo

    An object of class `phylo` representing the tree to plot.

    pred_hosts

    A data.frame containing tip information with three columns: - `label`: character vector of tip names (species names matching tip labels). - `is_known`: logical vector indicating if the tip is a known host. - `is_pred`: logical vector indicating if the tip is a predicted host.

    label

    Character string indicating the column name in `pred_hosts` containing the tip labels.

    layout

    Character string specifying the tree layout (default: `circular`).

    tiplab_offset

    Numeric, offset distance of tip labels from the tree (defaut: `5`).

    tiplab_size

    Numeric, font size of tip labels (default: 1.7).

    tippoint_shape

    Numeric, shape code for known host tip points (default: `18`).

    tippoint_size

    Numeric, size of the tip point symbols (default: 2).

    pred_color

    Character, colour for predicted host labels (default: `darkgoldenrod3`).

    nonpred_color

    Character, colour for non-predicted tips (default: `gray50`).

    known_color

    Character, colour for known host tip points (default: `#cf3530`).

    show_legend

    Logical, whether to show a legend (default: `FALSE`).

    Value

    A `ggtree` object that can be printed or further customised.

    Examples

    pred_hosts <- data.frame(
  quercus_sp = oak_phylo$tip.label,
  is_known = oak_phylo$tip.label %in% known_hosts,
  is_pred = oak_phylo$tip.label %in% pred_hosts
)
#> Error: object 'oak_phylo' not found
plot_oak_phylo_hosts(oak_phylo, pred_hosts, label = "quercus_sp")
#> Error in plot_oak_phylo_hosts(oak_phylo, pred_hosts, label = "quercus_sp"): could not find function "plot_oak_phylo_hosts"
